listen_host.description: IP address to bind to (empty string means all interfaces).

pop3_port.description: Port number to listen on for unencrypted POP3.

pop3s_port.description: Port number to listen on for POP3 over SSL/TLS.

imap_port.description: Port number to listen on for unencrypted IMAP.

imaps_port.description: Port number to listen on for IMAP over SSL/TLS.

ssl_cert_file.description: Path to the SSL/TLS certificate file.

ssl_key_file.description: Path to the SSL/TLS private key file.

ssl_protocols.description: List of allowed SSL/TLS protocols (modern safe defaults recommended).

backend.description: Backend method for resolving user credentials and mailbox locations.

perdition_map_file.description: Path to perdition map file (used only when backend = 'file').

ldap_url.description: LDAP server URL (used only when backend = 'ldap').

ldap_bind_dn.description: DN to bind as when connecting to LDAP (used only when backend = 'ldap').

ldap_bind_password.description: Password for LDAP bind DN (used only when backend = 'ldap').

ldap_search_base.description: LDAP base DN for user searches (used only when backend = 'ldap').

ldap_user_filter.description: LDAP filter for user lookup (used only when backend = 'ldap').

ldap_group_filter.description: LDAP filter for group lookup (optional, used only when backend = 'ldap').

db_host.description: Database host name or IP (MySQL/PostgreSQL backend).

db_query.default: SELECT home,uid,gid FROM users WHERE username = '%u'
db_query.description: SQL query for user lookup (MySQL/PostgreSQL backend).

max_clients.description: Maximum number of simultaneous client connections.

timeout.description: Connection timeout in seconds for idle clients.

log_facility.description: Syslog facility or file path for logging.

user.description: System user to run the process as.

group.description: System group to run the process as.

backend_entries.description: Optional additional backend definitions (for virtual domains or multi-tenant setups).

name.description: Identifier for the backend (e.g., domain name).
